Kristen Hawkins

Democratic candidate for Supreme Court, Place 7, Texas

Presiding Judge, 11th District Court, Harris County

Kristen Hawkins is a Democrat and the presiding judge of the 11th District Court, a civil court in Harris County. Before becoming a judge she spent 18 years practicing law, ran her own practice and served as a tax master (special master) for five years. She defeated Gordon Goodman in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and faces incumbent Republican Justice Kyle Hawkins (no relation) for Place 7 on November 3, 2026.

Where Hawkins stands

Judicial philosophy
Says her judicial philosophy is to apply the law equally to everyone who appears in court, so that results are consistent and predictable regardless of a party's financial resources.
Right to jury trial
Supports preserving Texans' constitutional right to a trial by jury and respect for jury verdicts. Says appellate courts should be cautious about overturning jury verdicts.
Case selection / court docket
Proposes that the Supreme Court choose cases that matter to all Texans, not only to well-resourced litigants.
Trial-court experience on the high court
Argues the Supreme Court would benefit from the view of district judges, who apply its rulings and see how they affect parties, lawyers and access to the courts.

Background

  • Judge, 11th District Court, Harris County (first elected 2016; on the bench since 2017; current term ends 2028)
  • Oversaw multidistrict litigation, including the Astroworld lawsuits
  • Tax master/special master for part of Harris County, 5 years
  • Private law practice, 18 years in total, including her own Social Security disability practice
  • Board-certified in civil trial law and personal injury law
  • Tex-ABOTA Judge of the Year, 2021
  • J.D., magna cum laude, South Texas College of Law Houston
  • B.A., University of Texas at Austin
